commits.edited_message:
htj2k: Check for duplication file_index values when reading file header (#2516)

Non-strict header parsing takes the attribute and channel name limit
from the width of the context's max_name_length field, and from
EXR_LONGNAME_MAXLEN when that maximum is larger. Strict parsing is
unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Pierre-Anthony Lemieux <pal@palemieux.com>

Fix/suppress compiler warnings (#2582)

- unused variable in PyOpenEXR_old.cpp
- (void*) cast in read.c
- all.cpp: suppress unused variable warnings altogther since this is
  example code for the website
- store context max_name_length as uint16_t

max_name_length is assigned to and from int32_t name lengths in the
header parser and in exr_set_longname_support. Keeping the field (and
the locals that mirror it) a uint8_t forced a narrowing conversion at
each of those sites.

Signed-off-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

Misc warning cleanup (#2626)

* remove useless functions

these used to print, but the prints were removed and are now extraneous

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* use double brace struct initializer (warning cleanup)

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* add inline tag (warning cleanup)

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* add additional build folder ignores

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

* raise the long-name limit from 255 to 511

A part name and a channel name are concatenated in some multipart
files and no longer fit in the historical 255-character cap. Name
lengths on disk are int32, and the context stores the limit in a
field wide enough for the larger value.

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Kimball Thurston <kdt3rd@gmail.com>
commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_constants.h b/src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_constants.h
index 84c788b..304ce77 100644
--- a/src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_constants.h
+++ b/src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_constants.h
@@ -26,6 +26,6 @@
  */
 
 #define EXR_SHORTNAME_MAXLEN 31
-#define EXR_LONGNAME_MAXLEN 255
+#define EXR_LONGNAME_MAXLEN 511
 
 #endif /* OPENEXR_PRIV_CONSTANTS_H */

coupling: The stack overflow in read_text's 256-byte name buffer is reachable from any two of the three edits, and from none of them alone. 006cdab stops taking the non-strict name limit from the (possibly truncated) max_name_length field and instead uses the full range of that field's type, or EXR_LONGNAME_MAXLEN when that constant is larger. With the original uint8_t field and a long-name maximum of 255, that range is 255, so the write in read_text stays inside text[0..255]. 5ec4604 widens max_name_length and the exr_set_longname_support locals from uint8_t to uint16_t but does not change the numeric limit. Alone the parser still uses 255. Together with 006cdab, sizeof(max_name_length) becomes 2 and the helper's range becomes 65535, so pull_attr writes text[256]. 586aadb raises EXR_LONGNAME_MAXLEN from 255 to 511. Alone the assignment into the uint8_t field truncates 511 to 255, so behavior is unchanged. Together with 006cdab the helper compares that constant as an int32 and lifts the limit to 511. Together with 5ec4604 but without the helper, the widened field stores 511 and the original maxlen = ctxt->max_name_length path overflows the same buffer. Reverting any one edit leaves a crashing pair: drop the helper and the wide field still holds 511; narrow the field back to uint8_t and the helper still promotes EXR_LONGNAME_MAXLEN 511; restore the constant to 255 and the helper still uses the uint16_t range. The overflowing store is the pre-existing text[namelen] write in read_text, which none of the three diffs touches, so a repair has to reconcile the limit helper, the field width, and the raised constant with that unchanged buffer.
